messages:
nina: Filing a heads-up from support: samplekit sample app hit a production crash after a fncall in JSON mode. Root cause looks like SDK helpers disagreeing on how to treat nullable arrays.

paul: can you paste the minimal output and the schema that triggered it?

nina: minimal model output: ```json
{"items": null}
```
schema excerpt: ```yaml
properties:
  items:
    type: ["array", "null"]
    items:
      type: string
```

zoe: summary of parity we saw locally: JS helper coerces null -> [], Python returns null, Go SDK turns it into a nil slice which later panics in our templating layer (`template: execute: nil pointer deref`).

raj: oh interesting — why is Go different? Is it a marshal/unmarshal quirk?

paul: yes, Go's json.Unmarshal maps null -> nil slice, Node helper has an explicit normalize pass that replaces nullish arrays with [] to be friendlier to older sample apps. Python intentionally left it alone to be strict. That divergence is the root cause.

nina: extra wrinkle: the auth/retry wrapper re-parses responses on retry and the node helper runs normalization twice in some code paths, which gives nested arrays for some outputs in older sampleapps (eg `[[]]`). Noticed on 2 customer incidents.

zoe: reproduction notes I left in the ticket: 1) model returns `{"items": null}`; 2) node helper -> `[]`; 3) retry wraps and parser runs again -> `[[]]`; 4) template expects strings and crashes or silently renders wrong output.

paul: suggested path forward: 1) make helpers preserve raw nulls by default (strict mode), 2) add a temporary SDK config flag `coerceNullables: true` for backwards compatible behavior that we deprecate after 1 release, 3) ensure normalization only happens once (idempotent).

raj: I like that. Also add an opt-in feature in Redwood Console and samplekit examples showing how to migrate schemas. We should prefer explicit schemas rather than relying on coercion.

nina: can CI add an integration test for the auth/retry + fncall path so the double-normalize never regresses?

ci-bot: ci-bot: created ci job DE-5130: sdk/compat/fncall-idempotence + flaky-run on PRs. Link: https://ci.redwood/DE-5130

zoe: small implementation note for SDKs: move normalization into the JSON-mode parser immediately after raw string -> object parse, then mark object with `_normalized=true` (internal symbol) so higher-level wrappers skip further normalization. That avoids the double-run without changing public behavior.

paul: for Go SDK specifically we should avoid adding sentinel markers on the object (not idiomatic). Instead, ensure the parser returns an internal typed wrapper that signals downstream code it has been normalized. Also update SDK docs for go/js/py parity table.

nina: docs/migration: add a short checklist in onboarding: 1) verify schemas use explicit nullability where intended; 2) run samplekit lint rule (WIP) that warns when schema uses `array | null` and your code assumes non-null; 3) set `coerceNullables` if immediate compat needed.

raj: I'll prototype the schema-lint rule in samplekit. Idea: static analysis of schema + code comments/typing to guess mismatch and warn. Could save a lot of support time.

paul: I opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 — implements idempotent parsing, adds `coerceNullables` flag, and unit tests across js/py/go. Please review.

zoe: quick ask: can we update onboarding sampleapp templates to use `[]` defaults instead of `null` where it makes sense and call out the difference in the migration guide?

nina: yes will update sampleapp and onboarding doc page once PR merges. Also will add a short note in the SDK changelog about behavior change and the deprecation plan for the flag.

paul: putting a small follow-up: add an e2e test that runs a real model mock, forces a retry path, and asserts the final object shape is stable (idempotent). That should have prevented the customer case.

ci-bot: ci-bot: linked issue DE-5130 to support ticket S-2981 and created a backport reminder for v1.9.x.

nina: thanks all. tagging @laura in case onboarding playbook needs a line. closing for now.
